Subject: Performance constraints and topology options for StorageMinds — next steps

Hi Maria —

Thanks again for a great call today. Quick recap and a proposed way forward so we have alignment before the technical deep-dive. I kept this intentionally short with clear asks.

Summary of pain points you called out
- Large variance in latency during peak ingest windows (spikes to several seconds at the tail).
- Cost per token is high for the current model footprint; need predictable per-request economics.
- Cold-starts and cache churn when traffic shifts between regions.
- Requirement: data residency for EU customers (may impact routing) — noted for later.

Goals (what success looks like for StorageMinds)
- User-facing P95 generation latency <= 150 ms for 256-token responses; P99 <= 400 ms.
- Sustained throughput of ~350 qps for the inference tier (90% of daily traffic).
- Predictable unit cost with ability to cap effective spend during spikes.
- Multi-region redundancy with failover within 500 ms for routing.

Model / inference requirements we discussed
- Primary model: 13B-class quantized (mixed INT8/FP16) for most user flows.
- Fallback: 70B opt-in for long-form analysis jobs (batched offline or queued).
- Average prompt length: 120 tokens; average generation 80 tokens. Peak seq length up to 2048 for some Analysis jobs.
- Expect KV-cache reuse rate to be ~30% on average; certain prompt patterns (templates) should be highly cacheable.

Topology options (tradeoffs)
1) Hosted + Dedicated pool (recommended starting point)
   - Redwood hosted control plane, dedicated GPU pool reserved for StorageMinds. Predictable throughput and latency SLOs without managing infra.
   - Autoscale with burst buffer: keep 20% headroom for short surges.
   - Good fit if you want fast onboarding and a single control plane.

2) Dedicated (customer-owned VPC peering)
   - Dedicated GPUs in a customer VPC or peered subnets (recommended if you need strict network controls).
   - Allows tighter egress controls and localizing KV cache inside your VPC to reduce tails.

3) Private (on-prem or air-gapped)
   - For regulated workloads; full control but larger ops burden. Consider only for specific EU/financial customers.

Performance mitigations we will apply
- Prefetch and prefix/KV cache with policy tuned to your prompt templates. Should reduce token compute by ~15–30% for conversational flows.
- Dynamic batching tuned to keep latency below the P95 target at target qps.
- Model routing by cost/latency: route high-priority queries to faster model variants; background analysis to batch-optimized hosts.
- Fallback policies: degrade gracefully to smaller quantized models when tail capacity is constrained.

Proposed next steps (owners + dates)
- StorageMinds (Maria): provide 48–72h sample traffic (scoped anonymized prompt set + token distribution) — target May 3.
- Redwood (Camila + Hiro): run an internal perf run against a 13B quantized profile and share projected throughput/cost delta — target May 5.
- Schedule 90-minute technical deep-dive (SRE + ML infra) to validate topology and test harness: propose Tue May 2, 11:00 AM PT — please confirm.
- Camila to produce a 1-page ops checklist (deploy knobs, KV cache parameters, autoscale headroom) after the perf run.

Attachments: topology-options.pdf (one-page decision matrix), kv-cache-profiles.xlsx (sample cache hit profiles) — both attached for reference.

If all that aligns, I’ll have Camila prepare the perf run and cost sensitivities; Hiro will scope the model quantization/latency tradeoffs for the 13B pipeline.

Thanks again — appreciate the clarity on goals today.

-Jordan
